anchor.quote: Let $m$ be the dimension of the ambient label space, a fixed number.
Let $W$ be the number of wires in the network, which is also the number of roles among which the rows of the array are distributed.
Let $V$ be the number of stored data bits in the array that the call works on.
Let $f$ be the parameter of the call, the number of digits in the address field being interchanged, or the number of selected axes in a numerical layer.
Let $s$ be the total number of smaller calls that one call makes.
Let $N$ be the sum of the dimensions of the labels at the sources,
and let $L$ be the total dimension lost along decreasing edges
Let $g(f)$ be the cost of a call at parameter $f$ divided by its volume.

gaps.quote: or the number of selected axes in a numerical layer.
gaps.note: The page uses 'numerical layer' to define the parameter f but neither explains it nor links it to another page, so the reader cannot tell what f counts in that case.

gaps.quote: The rows are split into role streams by, so every stream has the same size
gaps.note: The sentence stops at 'by' and never says how the rows are divided into streams, so the reader cannot check that every stream has the same size, and the claim that a call at parameter mf reduces to calls at parameter f on streams of volume V/W depends on it.

gaps.quote: so the number of smaller calls is governed by the dimension changes of the labels along the edges
gaps.note: The page says calls are counted on the wires of the subset-intersection network but does not explain how a call is assigned to a wire or edge, so the reader cannot check why s is governed by label dimension changes.

gaps.quote: Summing the absolute dimension changes over all edges gives $Wm - 2N + 2L$
gaps.note: The identity is justified only by 'since the signed sum plus twice the lost dimension', which the page does not expand; the reader cannot check the arithmetic relating the absolute sum, the signed sum and L.

gaps.quote: Depending on the construction, $s$ equals $Wm - N + 2L$ or $Wm - 2N + 2L$
gaps.note: The page does not say which construction gives which formula, nor derive either one, so the reader cannot check the stated value of s or the bound it implies.

gaps.quote: The paper shows that, so $2L < N$ and hence $s < Wm$.
gaps.note: The inequality 2L < N is attributed to 'the paper' without naming or linking it and without showing the argument, so the key step s < Wm cannot be checked from the page.

gaps.term: iterating to a power of f
gaps.quote: and iterating the relation gives $g(f) \approx f^{\tau}$
gaps.note: The page does not say how the relation is iterated, that f must be a power of m, what the starting value of g is, or how much the approximation sign hides, so the reader cannot check that g(f) is about f to the power tau.

gaps.term: tau below one needs m greater than one
gaps.note: Taking the logarithm base m turns s/W < m into tau < 1 only when m is greater than one, which the page never states; the reader cannot check this step from what it gives.
